html:
A great reservoir in the dry zone of Sri Lanka, built by King Dhatusena of Anuradhapura around 460 CE.

An earth dam several kilometres long held back the water. A canal, the Jaya Ganga, carried it some 87 kilometres to the capital, on such a gentle slope that it counts as a fine piece of ancient surveying. It filled the city's tanks and watered rice fields along the way. Water works like this let the kingdom grow rice in a land of long dry seasons.

The chronicles tell a grim story about it. Dhatusena's son Kashyapa seized the throne and asked his father where the royal treasure was. The old king led him to Kala Wewa, said that this was all his wealth, and was put to death. Kashyapa then built his fortress at Sigiriya. The reservoir was restored in modern times and still serves farmers.
sum: A great reservoir in the dry zone of Sri Lanka, built by King Dhatusena of Anuradhapura around 460 CE.
